name: Optimize cpu_throughput (msgs/sec) without regressing hot-path & cache benches

description: Baseline with .auto harness. Bench-profile throughput ~468k msgs/sec (release+lto direct run was ~500k; harness uses cargo bench profile consistently). All checks pass.

asi.notes: Bench profile (no lto) vs release profile differ ~7%. All measures use cargo bench profile. cpu_throughput bench runs 1 warmup + 3 timed batches of 10k simple posts; fixtures have no reply/embed/facets.

description: Reuse simd-json Buffers across messages: added parse_message_batch + parse_message_with_buffers; throughput bench now parses the whole batch with one shared Buffers. Eliminates per-message allocation of input_buffer/string_buffer/structural_indexes/stage2_stack (~5 allocs/message). Throughput 468k→628k (+34%). parse_message single-path unchanged (Buffers::new(len) like from_str).

asi.hypothesis: reusing simd-json Buffers across messages removes per-message internal scratch allocation
asi.insight: per-message simd-json Deserializer construction was ~40% of parse cost (5 allocs/message incl aligned input_buffer)
asi.next: wire shared Buffers into production ws ingestion loop too
asi.result: +34% throughput, tier-1 parse bench unchanged (no regression)

description: Hydrate single-pass: resolve_profiles now returns cached profiles via one bulk get_user_profiles (no contains_key pass), hydrate_one reads a HashMap<&str,Arc> and is sync (no per-message moka get / await). Throughput noisy (567k this run, 609-628k in others) but hydration benches improved: single_message_hydration 910→884ns, batch 12.0µs vs 13.6µs baseline. Tests updated minimally (2 assertions on resolve_profiles return shape).

asi.hypothesis: one cache pass instead of contains_key+get, sync hydrate_one
asi.insight: machine is noisy (load avg 2.5-3.0, M4 Pro); throughput swings 560-640k for identical code. A/B of this change was within noise; hydration microbenches improved measurably
asi.next: wire shared Buffers into production ws ingestion loop; attack encode phase (2 allocs/message, 512B caps)
asi.noise_floor: ±10% on throughput; median-of-5 batch runs still noisy

description: Production parity: ws ingestion loop now reuses one simd-json Buffers across all messages on a connection (parse_message_with_buffers), avoiding per-message parse scratch allocation in production (bench already measured batch parse). Sqlite store buffer-reuse experiment REVERTED — sqlx Query holds &str bind borrows across rows so a shared buffer can't be reused there; kept owned to_string in store path (encode allocs inherent to sqlx bind API).

asi.hypothesis: production ws loop should benefit from shared Buffers like the batch parse
asi.insight: sqlx Query::bind with &str keeps the borrow alive across rows, so reused scratch buffers can't feed sqlx binds; owned Strings required in store path (reverted). Encode allocs structural to sqlx.
asi.next: attacks: (1) reduce per-message hydrate overhead further; (2) record Value tree in parse/encode; (3) reduce noise by pinning/lowering system load
asi.noise: throughput swings 566-655k for same code; treat single-run deltas <10% as noise

description: Switch hydrate-phase HashSet/HashMap to ahash hasher (already a dependency via moka). Batch dedup, profiles_by_did map, post_outcomes map now use ahash RandomState instead of SipHash. Hydrate phase 4.5ms→3.4ms per 10k; throughput medians 636-666k across direct runs (+40% vs baseline). single_message_hydration 910→826ns, batch hydration 13.6→11.5µs. All tier-1/tier-3 secondaries within noise. Added sqlite_store_record/sqlite_batch_store as tracked guards.

asi.hypothesis: ahash faster than SipHash for short-string keys in batch dedup/maps
asi.next: parse phase (4.8ms) and encode phase (4.9ms) are now the biggest; record serde_json::Value tree walk is the likely remaining structural cost in both
asi.note: measure.sh now guards sqlite_store_record (42µs) and sqlite_batch_store (493µs)

description: Change CommitData.record from Option<serde_json::Value> (BTreeMap-based) to Option<simd_json::OwnedValue> (ahash HashMap-based, O(1) get). Added owned_record() helper for constructions. RecordView now operates on OwnedValue (record_view_extract_refs 118ns→31ns, -74%). parse_message_simd_json 2.34→2.12µs. Throughput 660k→676k median-of-3. single_message_hydration 826→815ns, batch 11.5→10.6µs. All checks pass; ~12 construction sites migrated (fixtures, benches, server/redis tests, integration tests).

asi.hypothesis: serde_json::Value record uses BTreeMap build (slow) and BTreeMap get; simd_json::OwnedValue uses ahash HashMap — cheaper build + O(1) get
asi.next: remaining phases: parse ~4.7ms, encode ~4.9ms, hydrate ~3.4ms. parse copy (to_string) unmeasurable in bench; encode allocs structural to sqlx
asi.note: OwnedValue::Object serializes in hash order (non-deterministic across processes) — no exact-string comparisons in tests depend on record key order
asi.win: tier-1 parse benches IMPROVED (record is the big subtree in those fixtures); record_view_extract_refs -74%; batch hydration improved

description: Drop MessageContext.author_did String (use message.did directly: 1 fewer String alloc/message); profiles_by_did keyed by Arc<str> cloned from the profile's own did (refcount bump, no string copy) with &str lookup via Borrow; make cache/resolver profile+post bulk APIs generic over AsRef<str>. Throughput within noise of prior state (664k vs 676k; direct runs 617-701k) but single_message_hydration 815→766ns, code simpler. get_user_profiles/resolve_profiles/resolve_posts now accept &[&str] or &[String].

asi.hypothesis: remove author_did String alloc; Arc<str>-keyed profile map avoids copy
asi.insight: measurement noise (±5% on median-of-3) makes sub-5% changes hard to verify; hydrate microbenches improved (766ns vs 815ns)
asi.next: encode phase ~4.9ms is now the largest; parse ~4.3ms; hydrate ~2.9ms. Try: owned-parse (production-only, unmeasurable here), encode allocs are sqlx-structural

description: Final verification of committed state: 730k msgs/sec (+56% vs 468k baseline). simd_json_serialize_record verified with full criterion (100 samples): -0.2% and -1.5% change (no regression — the +2.1% in the short-sample run was noise). All checks pass (190 lib tests + 6 integration tests). All tier-1/tier-3 secondaries within CI thresholds; parse benches -11%/-13%, record_view_extract_refs -75%, batch hydration -24%, single_message_hydration -16%.

asi.next: remaining levers are <3% each or production-only (owned-parse for ws loop — see ideas.md); encode near structural limit
asi.summary: Kept: shared parse Buffers (+34%), hydrate single-pass, ahash maps, OwnedValue record (-75% record_view), author_did removal. Reverted: sqlite buffer reuse (sqlx borrows).

description: JetstreamMessage.did: String → Arc<str> (same type as BlueskyProfile.did). Hydrate dedup HashSet now stores Arc<str> (Arc::clone instead of String copy); profiles_by_did keys interoperate directly; cache.set_user_profile in fixtures uses to_string. Machine load spiked (2.5→5.4) during measurement so primary is noisy (652k measure vs 678-705k direct runs), but hydration benches improved: single_message_hydration 766→741ns, batch 10.35→9.92µs. ~25 construction/assertion sites migrated (tests, benches, server, storage, recovery).

asi.hypothesis: Arc<str> did removes per-message String copy in hydrate dedup; aligns with profile.did type
asi.insight: machine load spiked 2.5→5.4 during this run; primary measurement unreliable (±10%). Hydration microbenches (direct code measurement) improved 3-4%
asi.next: wait for load to drop before trusting primary deltas; remaining ideas are ≤3% or blocked (record raw-capture)

description: Native owned-DOM parse (to_owned_value_with_buffers + by-value field extraction via HashMap::remove) replaced the serde bridge in parse_message_with_buffers. RESULT: significantly SLOWER — parse phase 4.3ms→7.5ms (+70%), throughput 518k vs ~660-705k, parse_message_simd_json 2.29µs vs 2.08µs. simd-json's stage3 tape→owned-DOM conversion is far slower than the serde bridge for small messages. REVERTED to serde bridge (git checkout HEAD). All tests pass in both versions.

asi.hypothesis: native owned-DOM parse avoids serde dispatch overhead
asi.insight: do NOT replace the serde bridge for small structs; simd-json's serde path stays
asi.next: parse remains ~4.3ms; remaining levers are the extraction redundancy (~2%) and production-only wins (owned-parse)
asi.result: WRONG — stage3 tape→DOM conversion is ~1.7x slower than the serde bridge for small messages; parse 4.3→7.5ms. Reverted.

description: Merge extract_mentioned_dids_from_view + extract_post_uris_from_view into single extract_refs_from_view (one RecordView pass: reply_refs/embed_record_uri each traversed once instead of twice; ~2 fewer HashMap gets/message). Cleaner code, identical semantics. Hydration benches improved to best-yet: single_message_hydration 740.7→731.8ns, batch 9.92→9.69µs. Throughput 631k median-of-3 (direct runs 644-720k, load ~3.3).

asi.dead_end_recorded: native owned-DOM parse is ~1.7x SLOWER than simd-json serde bridge for small structs (experiment #10 discarded)
asi.hypothesis: shared reply/embed traversal in ref extraction removes redundant HashMap lookups per message
asi.next: all remaining levers now ≤2% (below reliable detection) or production-only (owned-parse for ws loop) or blocked (record raw-capture). Consider final verification + summary

description: Production ingestion win: ws loop now parses the owned Message::Text String directly via parse_message_owned_with_buffers (no text.to_string() copy — simd-json needs &mut, and the socket already hands us an owned String). The &str path is unchanged (still used by parse_message_batch and the hot-path bench). Parse-failure warn drops the raw-text preview (text consumed by owned parse) but keeps the parse error. Bench-neutral as expected (683.9k, best-of-band); all ws tests (malformed-frame recovery etc.) pass; production saves ~350B copy + alloc per ingested message.

asi.hypothesis: ws loop owns the String already; copy it only when the API requires &str
asi.insight: last documented production-only idea now implemented (owned-parse). All remaining levers are ≤2% or blocked
asi.result: bench-neutral (683.9k); real production win (~350B copy+alloc/message saved on ingestion)
asi.summary_of_session: 9 kept optimizations: shared parse Buffers, hydrate single-pass, ahash maps, OwnedValue record, did Arc<str>, author_did removal, combined ref extraction, ws shared Buffers, ws owned parse. 1 dead end measured (native DOM parse slower).

description: Serialize message+metadata into ONE buffer per record instead of two (sqlite store_record/store_batch + bench mirror). Production store_batch now builds all rows' combined JSON Strings first (1 alloc/row), then binds two &str slices of each (sqlx borrowed args outlive the query via the collected Vec<String>). Encode phase 4.9-5.2ms→4.5-4.7ms per batch; throughput 702.9k median-of-3 (best yet, +50% vs baseline); sqlite_store_record -5.9% and sqlite_batch_store -6.5% (full criterion, p<0.05 — IMPROVED, earlier short-sample upticks were noise); all checks pass.

asi.hypothesis: 2×512B serialize buffers per message → 1 combined buffer; sqlx Cow bind keeps borrowed &str slices valid if the owning Strings outlive the query (two-pass)
asi.insight: encode phase had ~2 allocs/message of allocator churn (profile: allocator ~18% of CPU). Halving them moved encode 4.9→4.6ms
asi.next: remaining: encode is now ~4.6ms and dominated by output-byte writing (structural); parse ~4.5ms (record tree + strings — data-bound); hydrate ~3.2ms (moka gets structural)
asi.verified: sqlite benches improved with full criterion (store_record -5.9%, batch -6.5%) — earlier short-sample +3% readings were noise

description: Bench measurement-faithfulness: cpu_throughput now parses owned Strings (parse_message_batch consumes Vec<String> via parse_message_owned_with_buffers — no input copy), matching production's ws-loop path exactly. The bench pre-builds TIMED_RUNS+1 pristine copies untimed and each run consumes one by value. Previously the bench measured the &str copy path production no longer uses, understating throughput by the per-message copy. Result: 699.6k median-of-3 (vs 702.9k prior — within noise; earlier 615k was load=4.4). All checks pass.

asi.hypothesis: bench should measure production's owned-parse path, not a stale borrowed path with an artificial copy
asi.insight: throughput is measurement-neutral in noise (699.6 vs 702.9k) but the bench is now faithful: the copy was already removed from production in the ws loop; the bench now reflects it
asi.load: spiked to 4.4 mid-session (615k reading); re-measured at 2.6 → 699.6k
asi.next: no further production-code changes pending; the bench now mirrors production parse exactly

description: Halve per-message monotonic reads in hydrate: hydrate_one now takes the previous record's completion Instant as its start (sequential records share the boundary; 1 Instant::now() read per message instead of 2 — ~10k reads/batch saved). hydrate_one returns (record, end_instant) which the loop threads forward; hydration_time_ms semantics preserved (wall time attributable to this record in the sequential batch). Hydration benches at best-yet: batch 9.37µs (from 9.86), single 728ns. Throughput 655k median-of-3 at load 3.3 (direct runs 630-705k — in the noisy band). All checks pass.

asi.hypothesis: sequential records share one boundary clock read per message (profile: mach_absolute_time in top CPU samples)
asi.insight: hydration microbenches improved to best-yet (batch 9.86→9.37µs) confirming the change; throughput noisy band 630-705k at load 3.3
asi.next: no remaining concrete measurable levers; encode ~4.5ms (output-byte bound), parse ~4.9ms (data-bound serde bridge), hydrate ~3.3ms (moka gets). Session at practical limit.
